r0.why: Name, Bezout, application of Euclidean division [1]; f(x)=f(r)+(x-r)*poly of degree one less [2].

r1.why: Remainder is f(r), x-r divides f iff f(r)=0, called factor theorem, all in [3].

r2.why: Quotient x^2-9x-27 and remainder -123 [4]; theorem gives f(3)=-123 [5].

r3.why: Formula matches Euclidean division [6], generalizes to any degree [7], also gives existence for this specific case [8].

r4.why: Evaluate f(r) via remainder R [9], long division harder than evaluating, synthetic easier [10], cheaper evaluation [11].

r5.why: Factor theorem as application, zero remainder means linear divisor is factor [12]; repeated use factorizes [13].
